testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A vehicle with air brakes is traveling at 55 mph in good conditions. How far does it need to stop completely?

options.text: 300 feet
100 feet
450 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when:

options.text: The brake shoes press against the outside of the drum.
The brake shoes press against the inside of the drum.
The brake shoes push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes press against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If brakes get too hot, what can happen?

options.text: The brakes may not work.
The brakes may squeak more than usual.
The brakes will brake unevenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may not work.
questions.explanation: Brakes can overheat and fade if used too much. When brakes fade, they lose stopping power. Drivers should also use engine braking to avoid overheating the brakes.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Press the accelerator.
Move the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the pedal can damage the brakes by combining spring force with air pressure.

questions.question: What system prevents the wheels from locking up during braking?

options.text: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)
Air brakes
An alternator

questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when brakes are applied.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To change the air pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving to remove these buildups.

questions.question: During an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Veer the trailer to the right and stop.
Stop in a straight line.
Veer the trailer to the left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: Use controlled braking or stab braking to stop in a straight line. Keep the vehicle straight but be ready to turn if needed.

questions.question: Do not drive a vehicle if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.

options.text: One half
One third
One fifth

questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Check brake drums during your pre-trip inspection. Do not drive if any drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.
The front lights should flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning does not work during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work. This delay is called brake lag.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on a vehicle.
They store compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied of extra air after each trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that the brakes use. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do when the tanks reach 125 psi?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It releases air from the tanks.
It starts pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Is ABS on only one axle dangerous?

options.text: Yes, it can be dangerous.
No, you still have more control when braking.
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you still have more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on only one part of the vehicle still gives you more braking control than having no ABS. Brake normally when you have ABS.

questions.question: What turns on when you push the brake pedal?

options.text: Headlights
Turn signals
Brake lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake lights
questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure triggers an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the compressor pumps air into the tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the compressor pumps air into the tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor decides when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather.
They remove water and oil from the tanks.
They send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These can damage the brake system if they build up. Drain valves help remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.question: How long should it take for air pressure to build up in a single air system?

options.text: 15 minutes
12 minutes
Three minutes

questions.correctAnswerText: Three minutes
questions.explanation: In a single air system, pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi in about three minutes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?

options.text: 25 seconds
10 seconds
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When does air pressure enter S-cam brake chambers?

options.text: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
When the driver uses the emergency brake.
When the driver uses the trailer hand valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out rods and moves slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?

options.text: Water
Cardboard
Brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When driving downhill, you should brake until your speed is:

options.text: 5 mph below your safe speed.
10 mph below your safe speed.
15 mph below your safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, press the brake pedal until your vehicle reaches 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must designate which system you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. Both systems share the same brake controls. However, each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A low pressure warning device.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A low pressure warning device.
questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type of this device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air tank pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: Before driving down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.

options.text: Higher
Faster
Lower

questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Before going downhill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle speed up as you go down the hill.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Can be used to prevent a parked vehicle from moving.
Make it easier for a parked vehicle to roll.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used to prevent a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use a parking brake, wheel chocks can hold a parked vehicle in place on a level surface.
